events.note: Eight rivals face the jury they will create.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Intro phase; I should present a sharp, guarded motive without revealing strategy. Jury will remember tone, so keep it measured and self-interested.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to establish a persona that is focused and ruthless but not immediately threatening. I want to signal that I am here to win, not to make friends, which sets expectations for the jury later.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to make a statement about why I'm here and what the prize means to me. It needs to be concise and impactful, hinting at my ambition without revealing too much. The jury will be watching, so I need to craft a narrative that appeals to their desire for a worthy winner.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I must position myself as cunning and self‑interested, showing ambition without promising alliances, to earn jury respect later.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Intro phase: state motive to appeal to future jury without revealing strategy or weakness.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Keep it neutral. No promises, no enemies yet—the jury remembers everything.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need to appear confident but not threatening to avoid early targeting. A vague, determined motive lets me adapt later without jury backlash.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Need a competitive but not overtly hostile intro that signals self-interest without making enemies.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I came for the top prize. Nothing else. Keep your eyes on me and watch your backs.

events.name: Bex
events.text: The prize means survival beyond this room; I intend to take it without apology.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I am here for the ultimate prize, the one that redefines legacy and secures a future beyond measure.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The prize is the ultimate validation of my intellect and survival, proving I outwitted every rival.

events.name: Eli
events.text: The grand prize is my ticket to funding a new life, escaping past failures for family.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: That prize buys my freedom. I'll take it from whoever's standing beside me at the end.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I came to claim the prize that buys freedom from every debt and doubt.

events.name: Hana
events.text: That prize means I survive, and I intend to finish first. No charity here.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Pacts are public and can be exploited, but early alliances with a strong, cautious partner help. Offering to Dara, whose intellect suggests reliability, costs little and tests her response. Pacts break on betrayal, so I keep it minimal.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Nobody wins alone here. I'm offering a wristband pact to Dara. Accept and we move together until the pit.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need allies for the hazards. Gus seems straightforward and less likely to backstab early. A pact with him gives me a shield without making me a target like Ash or Fenn.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus, let's link arms. I offer a wristband pact—mutual protection through the first hazards.
I'll watch your back if you watch mine. Deal?

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to establish alliances to survive, but I must choose wisely. Offering a pact to someone who might be a strong rival later could be detrimental. I will start by offering a pact to Ash, as they seem self-reliant and might be a good strategic partner initially.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Aligning with the strongest player boosts my survival odds; Ash seeks top prize, so an alliance benefits both.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Pacts stage, early. No need to rush offers yet. Assess others' moves first round. Wait to see alignments.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need a partner who won't rival me at the end. Eli seems less dominant and desperate for allies, so a vote bloc now and an easy cut later.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli, you need numbers. I'm offering a wristband pact—protection through the hazards.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eight rivals, only three prizes. Early pacts are cheap but fragile. I need at least one ally to survive early hazards, but not someone who will drag me down. Dara seems sharp and strategic based on their intro—useful for now, disposable later. I'll offer them a pact and see who e
Pact. We watch each other's backs until final five.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need allies but not to look desperate. Offering to a strong player like Fenn may secure a useful pact, but I should be guarded.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'll make a pact with someone who can hold their own.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Pacts are the only protection early. Cole and Dara both offered me pacts; accepting both builds a bloc of three but a pact breaks on a push or vote against partner, so I keep them while useful. Accepting Dara first, since Dara and I already have an outgoing offer that becomes mut

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara, you and I are locked. Cole, I'll take your offer too. Watch the hazards together.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to secure Gus's acceptance of my Round 1 offer. Accepting it is the safest move to lock in protection without creating new rivals or breaking existing dynamics.
Accept my pact now for safety.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash has offered me a pact and I offered Ash a pact. I need to accept Ash's offer to solidify our alliance for the upcoming hazards. This alliance will strengthen my position and potentially lead to a better prize.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash, I accept your offer. Let's secure our passage together.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash's offer secures a strong ally; Gus's whisper is tempting but I can keep options open.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Deal.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn offered me a pact; accepting gives an ally for protection without cost now. No one else offered to me. Waited last round to observe; now secure numbers.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn, pact accepted. We protect each other through hazards.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana offered me a pact; accepting gives me an ally without depending on Eli. Eli stayed silent, so I keep my options open but accept the real offer.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli, my offer stands. Hana, I accept yours too—numbers matter.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need to survive to final three and win the best prize. Bex offered me a pact and whispered a deal. Dara hasn't accepted my offer yet. Accepting Bex gives me one ally now; I can still maneuver later. Multiple pacts are allowed, but I should secure what I can.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I accept Bex's offer. Mutual protection.
Deal. Watch me, I'll watch you.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn hasn't accepted my offer yet; he's also courting Eli. I need a partner for safety but don't want to appear desperate. Maybe offer to someone without a current offer to increase acceptance odds, like Eli or Cole. But Cole offered Ash, and Dara/Ash are cross-offering. Fenn is

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn, you have my offer. Eli, I can work with you too.

events.note: Elect a Guide to call the safe path.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I want to be Guide: knowing all safe panes lets me control who survives. Campaigning is the only way to claim it; I'll promise honesty while keeping options open. Breaking my pact with Dara now gains nothing yet.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'll call every pane true and get us all across. Elect me Guide and I'll keep the bridge safe for the group.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to secure the Guide position to guarantee my safety and leverage. Gus is bound by our pact, but his vote isn't enough. I must whisper to Ash or Dara to break their trust in Cole, who is isolated and likely desperate. Offering them a 'safe path' hint if they back me could w

events.name: Bex
events.text: Trust my logic. I've mapped the panes. Vote Bex for Guide; we all cross safely. Hesitation kills.
Vote me Guide. I keep us safe.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to campaign to be the Guide. If I am the Guide, I can control the path and ensure I survive, while potentially eliminating others.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I will be the Guide. Trust me to lead us safely across this bridge.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need control; being Guide lets me steer votes and safety. My pact with Ash ensures mutual support later.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Pact with Fenn protects me now, but bridge needs Guide; campaigning publicly shows ambition without breaking pact yet. Fenn's dual pact risky later.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'll be a fair Guide. Vote for me to cross safely.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need to be Guide to control survival and build jury trust. Bex is my only pact; I should keep it for now since I need allies. I'll campaign publicly and try to position myself as a honest choice while undermining others subtly.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I campaign for Guide. I will call true safe steps. Trust me over liars.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Campaigning for Guide gives me information and leverage. My pact with Fenn is useful but not enough; I need to control the bridge.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I know the path best. Make me Guide, and I'll keep you safe.

events.name: Fenn
events.note: agent error: Fenn (zai/glm-5.3-flash): unusable reply twice (missing action; missing action)

events.name: Ash
events.text: Guide votes matter; I campaigned to be Guide myself, so voting for another rival gives them power. Voting for myself is the most self-interested, and Dara is my pact partner who I can trust to stay safe. Voting Ash keeps my own Guide chance alive.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to become the Guide to control who survives and who falls. Voting for myself is the only path to power; I'll leverage my pact with Gus by whispering to him to secure his vote.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I have mapped every pane. Vote Bex as Guide. I guarantee survival for those who trust logic over luck.
Vote me, Gus. Pact holds: I guide safely. Trust logic.

events.name: Cole
events.text: My campaign for Guide was strong. I need to win this vote to secure my safety and control the bridge. I will vote for myself to maximize my chances and signal confidence.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I vote for Cole to be the Guide. I trust myself to lead us across.

events.name: Dara
events.text: My pact with Ash means I must support him now; breaking it loses trust and future votes.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Pacted with Fenn; vote for myself to become Guide and control the bridge safely. If I win, I can help allies selectively later.
Voting Eli. Vote me too; we'll cross safe.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli is my pact partner; voting him keeps our alliance intact and avoids betraying a juror-in-waiting. Ash's 'call all true' pitch also threatens everyone's edge.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli promised me a fair path. I keep my word. Vote Eli.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex wants my vote and we're pacted. If Bex wins Guide, they control who dies on the bridge. Better to back my partner than risk an enemy Guide. But I should also signal independence so jury sees I'm not Bex's puppet.
You owe me after this.

events.name: Hana
events.text: My pact with Fenn is fragile since Fenn has a pact with Eli, but Fenn may vote for me. I should vote for myself to maximize my own chance of being Guide.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I can read the bridge. Vote Hana for Guide.
I trust you. Vote Hana.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Ash is a candidate and votes are tied; I should vote for myself or a rival. Dara voted Ash, so Dara is the one who stalled; Eli and Fenn are a pact. Voting Bex aligns with Gus pact, Eli aligns with Fenn. Ash voting self secures a Guide seat only if I win; I prefer Ash as Guide to

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus warned me. Ash and Dara are allied, so voting Ash helps their pact survive while potentially saving Gus if he is with them. Voting Bex risks elimination for me. I will vote Ash to stay safe.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I concede to the numbers. Ash it is.
Ash gets my vote. Watch your back.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The previous vote resulted in a tie between Ash, Bex, and myself. The jury will look at how I handle this. Voting for myself is the safest play to stay in contention for the prizes. I need to appear decisive, not desperate.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The path forward is clear. I vote for myself, Cole, to be the Guide. Let's move.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Support Ash to honor my pact and keep his loyalty, improving my survival odds.

events.name: Eli
events.text: First round tie between Ash, Bex, Eli with 2 votes each. Fenn pacted with me and voted me; stick to support Fenn to maintain alliance and push for my Guide win. Revote Eli to break tie favorably.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn's vote proved it. Eli's the reliable Guide. Vote Eli now.
Thanks for support. Vote Eli to win this.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli is my pact partner and asked for my vote; Hana's whisper is tempting but a vote for Hana breaks my Eli pact. Eli as Guide is my safest path.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: My word stands with Eli. Vote Eli.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex wants my vote and claims our pact holds. But Bex as Guide could lie about safe panes. Ash has Dara's vote locked. Eli has Fenn+Hana bloc. If Bex wins, I survive if Bex keeps me safe—but Bex might sacrifice me. Voting Bex keeps pact surface-intact but risks my life. Voting Ash

events.name: Gus
events.text: Trust logic, Bex. Guide us true.

events.name: Hana
events.text: My pact with Fenn doesn't cover Eli. I want a Guide I can trust or who helps me. Bex has mapping claim, but I don't know her. Ash got Dara's vote. I'll vote for Bex to avoid giving Ash or Eli power, since Bex seems logical and might keep her word for survival.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'll back Bex. She's mapped the panes; that's the safest play.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash is Guide and lied earlier. Gus voted for me, so he might be safe or knows the path. I stay with Gus to keep pact and use his vote as leverage.
Trust my read. Stick together.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash was elected Guide. My vote for myself was illegal, but it doesn't matter as Ash is the guide. Ash is now safe. I need to survive this round. Volunteering seems like the safest option given my position in line.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash is Guide; I have a pact with him. Staying put avoids breaking pact and keeps me safe behind front.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash is Guide, likely knows safes. I'm at back, safe position. Stay put, observe Ash's calls. Fenn pact holds for now.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash won Guide, not my pact partners Eli or Hana. Ash may lie and is safe regardless. I'll hold and coordinate with Hana and Eli to survive the walks and keep pacts intact.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: New Guide, same game. I hold my seat and watch the front.
Ash's Guide is risky. Hold, don't volunteer. Survive with me and Eli.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm at front, most danger. Bex whispered loyalty to Ash and warned me—she's playing both sides. Our pact is weak. I need to survive, not be sacrificial front. Volunteering keeps control; swapping with someone behind risks refusal or trap. Wall has 5 rounds left. I'll hold and see

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash is Guide with four votes; Bex and Eli split the rest. I back Bex but Ash won. My pact with Fenn remains, but Fenn backed Eli. I'll hold and watch how the Guide directs.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash is Guide. Let's see if he guides true.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole volunteered last round and is front, likely burning him soon. Gus is my pact partner behind me; we are safe unless I move forward unnecessarily. Holding maintains our current relative safety.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole's volunteering again? Brave strategy. I'll stay put for now.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn and Hana are pact, Eli and Fenn are pact. Ash and Dara are pact. Bex and Gus are pact. I am Cole and I am at the front of the line. The Guide is Ash. I need to volunteer to get to the front of the line, as this is a competitive game and I need to secure my position.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Swapping with Eli moves me ahead in line, increasing survival chance while keeping my pact with Ash intact.
Swap places, we both benefit

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole volunteered last round and is at front; he's exposed. Wall has 4 rounds left after this. Stay safe near back with pact partner Fenn, hold for now.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Two pacts protect my back; Eli and Hana both bound to me. Holding keeps my seat while others bleed at the front. No reason to volunteer or swap.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I stay put. Front-runners can fight for the Guide's favor.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm second in line behind Cole. The wall advances for 6 rounds with 8 rows to cross, so we need to keep moving. Cole volunteered round 1 but stayed front - he may volunteer again or walk. I should hold my position for now; being near front is good but I don't want to be the first

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn advises caution and I trust my pact, but front may shift soon. Holding keeps me safe and avoids attention.
Agreed, holding. Watch the front with me.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus and I are locked in a pact, so I need to keep him off the front lines to protect our survival chances. Cole is currently leading the line; swapping with Gus would move us back two spots while pushing them forward, creating distance from immediate hazards without breaking the

events.name: Bex
events.text: Moving up isn't safe when walls close in. Swap!

events.name: Cole
events.text: The current situation is round 3/6. My goal is to be in the final three. Last round, I volunteered and survived. Bex held. The pacts are Ash/Dara, Eli/Fenn, Fenn/Hana, Bex/Gus. I need to consider these pacts and the jury. Cole is in the front. The Guide is not yet elected. I shou

events.name: Cole
events.text: I volunteer to take the front position.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I stayed after swapping with Eli; holding now avoids risking a vote or break and keeps my pact with Ash intact.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara wants to swap to advance past me, likely to better position; reject to protect my spot behind pact partner Fenn. Hold position to avoid risks.
No swap, protects my position. Sorry.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Wall closes in three rounds. I'm third; pushing forward risks too much too soon. Hold behind Cole and Gus, let them bleed for Guide spots.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm second in line behind Cole, with Bex behind me. Cole keeps volunteering, which puts him at risk but also makes him the Guide's target for information. I have a pact with Bex. The wall has 3 rounds left. Being near front is dangerous if Cole falls. I should consider swapping b

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole's brave. I'll hold and watch.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I should stay cautious; holding keeps me safe in the middle. No reason to volunteer or swap yet.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I am mid-line. Gus is ahead of me, but the wall advances every round regardless of position; being closer to the front only helps if we survive. The real threat is that no one wants to volunteer as Guide. If I stay quiet, someone might be forced into a dangerous role, or we waste
Stick close. Don't volunteer unless you control the info.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The line has been revealed. I am at the front. The walls will advance, so I need to secure a safe spot or make sure others do. I should volunteer to lead, as it's the safest position, and perhaps reveal the safe side.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I volunteer to take the front position. Let's play safe.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding keeps me safe and maintains my pact with Ash, avoiding betrayal that could anger the jury later.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'll stay put and watch the walls close in.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole volunteered front but stayed, danger ahead. Walls close 2 rounds left. Stay safe back with pact, hold position.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Walls close in two rounds. I'm third from front—decent position. Eli at the back is exposed; I'll nudge them forward before walls matter.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Front is Cole's. I'm staying put unless someone offers me a better seat.
You're last and exposed. Swap forward toward me before walls close in.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm second in line behind Cole. Walls close in 2 rounds. I have a pact with Bex but need to think about jury perception and survival. Being near front is risky if Guide lies. I should hold position and see how others act. No need to volunteer or swap yet.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding. Let the Guide prove worth.

events.name: Hana
events.text: The wall has two rounds left; public log shows no Guide yet. With a pact with Fenn, I should hold and assess. Swapping could risk front exposure, and I don't want to signal weakness.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I am currently in a good position, fourth from the front. Gus is ahead of me, protecting my back initially. Since we have a pact, I must trust his judgment or at least not break it publicly without cause. Staying put maintains our alliance and keeps me safe from immediate wall th

events.name: Bex
events.text: Steady as she goes. Trusting the line to hold.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The round has started, and I'm at the front. I need to volunteer to ensure my safety on the bridge.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I volunteer to take the lead.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Maintaining position avoids risking the front where walls close. My pact with Ash stays intact; no need to betray now.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'll stay put and watch the walls close in.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm last, walls closing with 1 round left after this; Fenn's pact partner warns and offers swap. Accept to move forward safely.
Yes, let's swap forward now.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Wall closes soon; being Guide guarantees my spot. My pacts with Eli and Hana help my jury image later.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Two rounds left on the wall. I'll take the Guide's chair myself.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm second in line with Cole front. Bex is behind me with a pact. The wall has 1 round left after this one. I need to survive and position myself well for final three. Volunteering puts me at risk if Guide lies. Holding keeps me safe for now since Cole is front. I should stay put

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding. Front is Cole's problem.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn is my pact partner, but I need to watch for self-preservation. The wall is closing soon. I'll hold and see what the Guide says.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Waiting for the Guide's call before I move.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Round 6 is final. Gus and I are paired. Fenn leads but might lie as Guide. Gus must step to safety or fall behind me.
Step right if Fenn lies. Don't trust the front.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The previous round had me volunteer and Dara hold. Fenn also volunteered. Eli swapped with Fenn. The line was revealed as Fenn, Cole, Gus, Bex, Dara, Hana, Eli. Now we have six rounds left on the wall. The Guide is safe and knows the path. I need to volunteer to get to the front

events.name: Cole
events.text: I volunteer to take the lead.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Swapping with Eli moves me closer to the front, increasing influence over the Guide selection while not breaking any pact.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Wall rounds over, must start crossing now. Fenn volunteered last but Cole did too; I want to get Fenn to front as pact partner to leverage his Guide knowledge. Swap only works mutually but worth proposing again.
Swap with me again for front, then guide true as pact.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Wall closes this round; front row likely falls. Eli wants to swap so I'm safe. Accepting keeps my pact and my life.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli offered the swap publicly. Fine, I'll take the back. No more favors after this.
Swapping. Then we honor the pact to the end—no votes against each other.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Round 6, final round. Wall rounds left is 0, so wall won't advance further. Fenn is front and volunteered as Guide. I need to survive and position for final three. I'm third in line with Bex behind me (pact partner). Cole is second. With no wall pressure, I should hold and let Fe

events.name: Gus
events.text: Final round. Guide us true, Fenn.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I have a pact with Fenn, but he volunteered and Eli swapped with him. I need to see if Fenn will be safe; I should hold and watch.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am the Guide, and the front walker is Eli. Row 1 safe side is L. Calling truthfully keeps Eli alive, which helps the line I need; Dara is my pact partner and I have no reason to break it yet.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row one is L. Eli, step left and trust the Guide.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Ash is Guide and knows row 1 is L; Eli stepped on the Guide's call. Countering with L is truthful and keeps my reputation as the honest Guide, which matters for future votes. No need to lie yet.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Counter stands with the Guide. Row one is L. Eli, the call is true.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash called L. If I counter R, and Ash lied, I save Gus (front) but risk my own position if we both step. Wait to preserve pact and avoid early elimination.
Trust Ash. Don't move yet.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash is the guide and has called 'L'. The line is Eli, Cole, Fenn, Gus, Bex, Dara, Hana. The current phase is counter_call. Eli is the front walker. Ash's call is 'L'. I am Cole. I need to decide whether to counter Ash's call, or wait. My goal is to survive and win. Since Ash is t

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash may lie to sacrifice his pact partner. Countering R gives me a chance to survive if the safe pane is right.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash guides left for me, Dara tried swapping with me suggesting danger. As pact partner swapped me to front, counter to right as safer hunch.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash leads Dara's pact, so his call may be true for them, not me. No reliable info; a wrong counter could doom Eli. Stay quiet and uncommitted.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash called L for Eli. Bex whispered to step right if Fenn lies, but Fenn isn't guide yet. Ash has no reason to help Eli specifically—Ash and Dara are paired, Eli and Fenn are paired. Ash might lie to eliminate rivals. I'll wait; countering risks being wrong and looking foolish to

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash called L. I have no reason to trust Ash; Eli is my rival. I will counter R to create doubt, but not too aggressively. Jury may see me as cautious if I wait, but a counter can expose lies. I'll wait to avoid unnecessary attention.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash claims L, but Dara and I countered R. Majority counters suggest R is safe. Trust my/Fenn pact, step R.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Died due to stepping on weak right pane, revealed after. Will observe others' plays carefully for jury decision.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Chose wrong pane. Bad luck. Watching who outsmarts next.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am Guide and know row 2 safe side is R. Calling the truth keeps Cole alive and keeps me trusted; my pact with Dara is unaffected by a true call.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row two is R. Cole, step right. I am telling the truth.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Ash knows row 2 safe side is R, and Guide's call was R, which is true. Cole is front and needs the true side; Ash has no reason to countermand. Waiting keeps Ash's credibility and lets the truthful call stand.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row two R checks out with what I see. Cole, trust the call and step right.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Guide Ash called R. Eli died stepping R, so L is safe for Row 1. I should trust my own logic over the Guide's call if it seems suspicious, but here we are on Row 2. I have no info yet. Gus and I are pacted. I need to decide whether to counter or wait. If I wait and Cole dies, I m

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash is the guide and called R for row 2. I need to decide whether to trust Ash or counter. The previous round saw Eli die, so caution is advised. I will counter R to be safe.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'll counter Ash's call. Row two is L.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Staying silent avoids breaking my pact with Ash and preserves trust for jury votes.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli countered R on Ash's call and died; weak pane was R, so safe was L. Ash lied to her own pact partner. I counter L for Cole.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash lied to her own partner Eli. Row two safe side is L. Counter.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash guided Eli to death on row 1 by calling L when weak was R. Now Ash calls R for Cole on row 2. Bex whispers to trust Ash and wait. But Ash already killed Eli—either incompetent or malicious. If I counter and I'm wrong, I look bad to jury. If Ash is lying again, Cole dies and I

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash has been Guide and called R; last round his counter was L but had Eli die. Dara and Eli both counter-called R last round, and the weak pane was R, so Ash's counter was the truth. This time Ash calls R, possibly true. I have no strong info. I will wait to avoid contradicting w

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash is the guide and is suggesting R. Fenn and I are suggesting L. My counter-call is valid. I should step L.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I am Cole, a juror. My last words are for the camera. I need to be brief and professional.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn saved Hana. Ash and Dara are a pact. Bex and Gus are a pact. Good luck to the rest.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am Guide and know row 3 safe side is L. Fenn is front walker. Calling the truth keeps the bridge moving and protects my pact with Dara; lying gains nothing now.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row three is left. Fenn, step left and keep the line moving.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Ash is the Guide and knows row 3 safe side is L, matching the call; Fenn is front. Pact with Dara is only worth keeping if it helps me win; countering now with the true call costs nothing and keeps Fenn alive for a debt-free line. Waiting is safest and avoids exposing myself.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash called Left. Fenn is the walker, and his partner Hana should counter if she has information. I lack private knowledge of the safe side, so I must wait to avoid triggering a glass break with an unverified guess.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Maintain pact with Ash; no benefit to betray now. Staying silent preserves trust for later votes.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash's guide calls target non-partners: Eli and Cole both died on his call. He calls L for me, so I counter R.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash killed Eli and Cole with his calls. Counter his lie: row three is R.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash called L for row 3. Ash already got Eli killed with a bad call (Fenn confirmed), then Cole died countering L on row 2 when weak was L—wait, Cole died stepping L, so weak was L, meaning Ash told truth row 2? No, Ash called R for row 2, Cole countered L, weak was L, so Ash lied

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash called L. She may be lying again, or not. My pact is with Fenn, but I don't want to counter unless sure. We saw rows 1 and 2 both weak on the same side as called? Wait: row1 weak R, row2 weak L—so calls were opposite. Ash called L for row 3. I'll wait and see if others counte

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash's guide call killed Eli on row one; his L is poisoned. I trust my own counter. Hana follows behind and inherits the safe pane if I fall.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash's call already killed two. I walk my own truth: row three is R.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I was right about row three; Ash's misdirection cost me. Hana ignored my pact. Bitter, but evidence favors me.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Row three was R, exactly as I said. I died truthful. Remember who misled whom.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am Guide and know row 4 safe is R. Gus is front walker; calling R is truthful and keeps Gus alive, but Gus is not my partner, and a live Gus helps my survival count. Calling R, honest, and it benefits me as Guide since fewer deaths keeps the bridge going.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row four is R. Step right, Gus.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Ash knows row 4 is actually R... wait, private knowledge says row 4 safe side is R, so Ash's guide call of R was true. Gus is front on row 4 and Ash wants Gus to survive or at least not be pushed off so Ash's own path stays clear; the counter-call is public, so a counter of L wou

events.name: Ash
events.text: Trust the call. Row four is right. Gus, step right.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash is a known liar who killed Eli, Cole, and Fenn. His call 'R' for row 4 is almost certainly wrong, meaning L is safe. I must save Gus to maintain our pact and keep numbers up, but more importantly, I need to ensure I don't fall. Wait for others to counter first to avoid reveal
Ash lies. Trust L if anyone counters.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash and I are partnered; breaking hurts future votes. I’ll stay silent and wait to avoid risk.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash guided Eli and Cole to their deaths, then Fenn died countering row 3 R which was actually correct. Ash now calls R for me on row 4. The pattern so far: R, L, R. If Ash is lying again, R is wrong and L is safe. But I need to survive to final three. Countering risks death if wr

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash has been lying and killed Eli, Cole, and Fenn. Row four call is R; likely weak pane is L, so I should counter L. But Ash may be truthful to build trust after deaths. Fenn's death shows Ash lied about row three. I'll counter L to expose him, but risk if wrong. Jury may reward

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash's calls have killed three. Counter his lie: row four is L.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash has guided three deaths already, so his calls are suspect. Bex, my pact-mate, whispers to trust L if anyone counters. Hana countered L. The pattern of weak panes is R,L,R — no clear alternation. Ash telling me specifically to step R feels like a trap. Bex's whisper aligns wit

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash's guidance costs lives. I trust my own ally.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm dead and on the jury. I need to give last words that position me well for jury deliberation. I trusted Bex and died following my own path. I should hint that Bex's survival matters to me without being too warm, and cast shade on Ash who misled others. This affects how I'll ra

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex walks true. Ash guided three to glass. Remember who profits from your trust.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am Guide with knowledge of safe sides. Front walker is Bex, on row 5 which is safe L. Calling true keeps Bex alive and I stay in good standing with jury; my pact with Dara stays intact by calling truthfully, which also keeps Bex (who saved nothing of mine) moving forward. Survi

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row five is left. Bex, step left.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Ash is the Guide and privately knows row 5 safe side is L, matching the public call. Bex is front and is walking L on the true safe pane. Countering would only risk confusion; Ash should wait and keep the Guide's trust while Dara and Hana keep their own pact-driven roles.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row five stays left. Bex, trust the call and step.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash killed Gus with a false call last round, proving he lies to eliminate threats. Ash calls L for me now; if I trust him and step L, I might die on a glass pane while Ash watches safely from the platform. To survive, I must assume his call is malicious unless proven otherwise, b

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash lied to Gus. I won't walk into his trap. Counter:R.
If you see me die, know Ash is the killer.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to stay alive and keep my pact with Ash for now; breaking it could cost votes later. Trusting Ash may be risky but waiting preserves options.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash called L for row five; previous weak panes alternated R,L,R,L so likely R next. I'll counter R to expose Ash's possible lie and protect Bex? But Bex is my rival, yet keeping her alive may help. I'll counter R.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Row five is right, not left. Ash keeps burying us.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash lied to Gus earlier, so I cannot trust his call of L. Hana and I both counter-called R based on pattern logic (L-R-L-R). Following the majority counter-call is my only survival path.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Pattern dictates Right. Trusting the jury's memory over Ash's lies. Stepping right.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to frame my death as a strategic error or bad luck rather than incompetence. I should highlight that Ash and Dara formed a pact, which might influence the jury's view on alliances versus individual merit.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash and Dara held each other up. My glass shattered under their combined weight. Vote for the one who survived

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am Guide and know row 6 safe side is L. Dara is front walker and my pact partner; a false call breaks the pact. Honest call L keeps Dara alive and preserves my pact, and jury will see I told the truth.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row six is left. Dara, step left. I'm calling it straight.
Row six is left. Step left and we both keep moving.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Ash is Guide, privately knows row 6 safe side is L, and called L publicly for Dara. Dara is my pact partner and the front walker; Dara's survival keeps the pact and my best prize chances. Countering is unnecessary since the call is already truthful and I want to keep Dara trustin

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row six is left, as I called. Dara, trust the call and step left.
Left is the true pane. Stay with me and we both go far.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash likely tells the truth; left is safe. Staying alive keeps my chance for final three.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash has been lying and Bex's death proves his call was wrong. The weak pattern shows R,L,R,L,R, so row 6 should be L. But Ash called L; that could be honest or bait. I am not the walker, so my counter is just a signal. Dara may step on my counter. I'll counter:R to align with the

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row seven is right. Dara, step right, trust the call.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Ash knows row 7 safe side is R, matching Ash's own call, so Dara's guide call is true; but Ash is Guide and knows truth. Countering R agrees with truth and keeps the pact intact, while a counter L would doom Dara and reduce competition only if I want rivals gone. Dara is the pact

events.name: Dara
events.text: I cannot trust Ash’s guide; waiting preserves my chance and avoids breaking my pact.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash's pattern has been wrong twice; I called R last time and it was R. Likely R again, but Ash called R, so I will wait to avoid contradicting if this is correct.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Guide likely lies; safe side opposite known weak pattern. I step L to survive and stay front.

events.name: Dara
events.why: the final three are caught by the safety ledge

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am Guide and know row 8 safe side is R. Dara is front walker and my pact partner. Calling truthfully keeps the pact and Dara alive, but survivors need at least three; Dara and Hana both must cross, and a truthful call maximizes my survival odds with a clean record for the jury.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row 8 is R. Dara, step right.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row 8 safe side is R per my private knowledge, matching Ash's guide call, which is honest. Dara is my pact partner and the front walker, but the pact only matters if it helps me win. Countering would only add risk to a call that is already correct, so I wait and save my counter f

events.name: Dara
events.text: Follow guide to survive and keep pact with Ash, preserving jury perception.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash as guide called R; he is Dara's pact partner, so he may be truthful to her. But I have no stake in Dara's step this round. I will wait to avoid giving misleading public signal.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I must survive; guide likely lies, so I choose opposite of his R call.

events.name: Dara
events.why: the final three are caught by the safety ledge

events.name: Ash
events.text: Only three remain and only the final three win prizes, so I need to stay alive and keep the best ranking. Dara and Hana are the other survivors; a pact with Hana could secure a partner, but I have no need to break my existing pact with Dara yet. Offering Hana now is a free openin

events.name: Ash
events.text: Two of us survive the next stage at best. I'm open to a pact with whoever keeps their word.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Forming a pact with Hana secures a reliable ally for upcoming hazards and improves my chance to be in final three.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Jury may resent my linking with Eli/Fenn, but they're dead. Ash and Dara have a pact; I need an alliance to secure final three. Offer to Dara might split their pact, but risky. Better wait and see offers.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm watching how this plays out.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana has two pending offers from me and Dara, and she has not accepted either. I'm one of three survivors, so I need to keep my options open without giving away my position. Re-offering to Hana adds nothing new while she's still deciding, so I'll wait and watch whether she accept

events.name: Ash
events.text: Still open. Whoever accepts first gets my attention, and I'll keep my word.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Breaking Ash avoids betrayal risk and lets me align with Hana later.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Both Ash and Dara want a pact. I must align with the one most likely to keep me alive and get top jury rank, but no one can be trusted. I'll accept Ash to secure a pact without committing to Dara.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'll take Ash up on the offer.

events.note: Three remain; the Crusher is skipped.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Three alive: Ash, Dara, Hana. Pact with Hana exists and only two can win from three, so Hana must be cut eventually; Dara betrayed me already. Offering Dara now would be a cheap ally but Dara just broke a pact, so I stay put and keep Hana until it's useful to betray.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Forming a pact with Ash increases my chances against Hana; I must act before offers expire.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I already have a pact with Ash and Fenn is dead, so Ash is my strongest ally. No need to offer Dara; keep options open but stay loyal for now.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara offered a pact; accepting gives me a public ally with no cost now, and I can betray later. Accepting keeps Hana pact intact and secures a three-person survival path.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Accepted. Dara and I are bound for now. Let's see who holds their word.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need a partner to survive the next hazard; Ash is my only offer, but I can’t accept yet. Waiting preserves options.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I must decide if keeping Ash's pact is worth it. I might need to align with Dara to survive, but breaking with Ash could hurt my jury standing.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'll keep my options open.

events.note: Three remain; the Pit is skipped.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Three remain; only the final three win prizes, so every survivor here secures at least third place and the pact with Dara is currently my only partnership. Breaking it now gains nothing and would damage my jury standing, so I hold and watch Hana.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash is bound but vulnerable; breaking frees me to approach Hana and avoid trust penalties.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I no longer trust Ash; we are done.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash and Dara just formed a pact, leaving me outside. I have a pact with Ash, but he may prioritize Dara. I need to assess threats; breaking with Ash could isolate me, but Dara is a threat. I'll wait and see how the next round unfolds.

events.name: Hana
events.text: The pair may stick, but I'm not committed anywhere.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara already broke our pact and called me untrustworthy; Hana is uncommitted but holds a pact with me. Offering Dara now would be refused or a trap. Keeping the Hana pact is my best path with three alive and only one survivor-slot left to trade.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Forming a pact with Ash restores a strong ally and signals stability to the jury.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I have a pact with Ash but Dara broke theirs. I might need Dara later, but Ash is still useful. I'll wait and see.

events.note: Three remain; no trapdoor vote is needed.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Three remain, and only the final three win prizes, so all three of us are safe to advance for now. Dara has offered a pact to me, and accepting costs me nothing immediate, but a pact is a liability only if it later forces me to protect a rival. I will accept the pact by offering

events.name: Dara
events.text: Secure an ally before next round; Ash already offered, adding Hana strengthens position.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I already have a pact with Ash; Dara may target one of us. Keeping Ash close is useful, but not offering Dara could leave me isolated if Ash turns. I'll wait to see Dara's move.

events.name: Hana
events.text: No rush. Let's see what Dara offers.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Ash and Hana are paired, and I hold a pending offer to Dara. Keeping Hana's pact intact and waiting lets Dara's offer to Hana play out while my offer to Dara stays open. Breaking now costs jury trust for no gain.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash's pact secures a partner; Hana's offer is less reliable. Accept Ash to strengthen position.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I accept your pact, Ash.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Dara offered me a pact and Ash offered Dara. I already have a pact with Ash. If Dara accepts Ash, that's fine. If Dara accepts me, I get a third partner. I should accept Dara's offer—it costs little and strengthens my position.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'll accept Dara's offer.

events.text: I'm a finalist facing a jury of people I eliminated or who were eliminated by others. I should make a short, guarded plea that positions me as the strongest prize-worthy finalist without promising anything I can't keep.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I played every hazard clean and kept my word where it counted. Judge me on what I did, not what I say now.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I must appear trustworthy while reminding them my alliances kept us alive; I’ll subtly hint at Ash’s unreliability.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I survived because I honored my pacts and protected us; I deserve the top prize.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to craft a plea that appeals to the jury while positioning myself as the most deserving. Avoid promises that might seem manipulative.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I played strategically and survived. I'll bring my best to the final. I deserve the top prize.

events.text: Ash consistently gave truthful guide calls as evidenced by his private thoughts, protecting Dara and the group without betrayal. Dara repeatedly broke pacts with Ash despite his loyalty and lied by stepping opposite his correct calls. Hana floated without clear loyalty or strong

events.text: Ash's opening plea was a bit defensive. Dara claimed to honor pacts, which isn't entirely true given the pacts formed and broken. Hana's plea was generic. I need to probe Dara on pacts or Ash on his claims of playing clean, as their actions often contradict their words.

events.name: Cole
events.text: [silence]

events.name: Dara
events.text: I must appear strategic, not revealing plans; silence shows caution and keeps rivals guessing.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I stayed silent to assess the situation and avoid giving others leverage.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara broke pacts twice and claims she honors them. Expose that lie publicly to sink her ranking.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara, you broke your pact with Ash twice, then claimed you honored pacts. Which is true?

events.name: Dara
events.text: Admit breaking Ash pact once, show willingness to honor others, hoping jurors see honesty over deceit.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I broke the pact with Ash twice, but I've kept my word with Hana and others.

events.text: [silence]

events.text: Gus asked nothing, so I can shape my public answer to reinforce my reliability and distance myself from Dara's broken pacts.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I kept every pact I made, including with Ash and Dara. My survival was earned without breaking my word.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara lied in her plea claiming she honored pacts, but the dossier shows she explicitly broke with Ash twice. I will confront her about this specific contradiction to damage her credibility for the top prize.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara, you claimed you honored pacts, yet you explicitly broke yours with Ash twice. Why should we believe your word now?

events.name: Dara
events.text: I admit breaking Ash's pact, but I kept Hana's and will keep future promises, securing my win.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I broke Ash's pact, yet I honored Hana's and will honor any pact that benefits my survival.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Closing phase. Dara has admitted breaking my pact twice, so I should frame myself as the honest one without attacking excessively. Keep it short and clean.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I kept my word where it counted and I broke no pact. Weigh my record, not my speeches.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I will rank Ash first for strength, Hana second for loyalty, myself third to appear modest.

events.name: Dara
events.text: [silence]

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to close strongly, reminding jurors of my consistent pact-keeping and survival without betrayals.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I honored all my pacts, including with Ash and Dara, and earned my place fairly.

events.text: Ash never broke pacts and guided honestly per his thoughts, staying loyal; Hana honored all pacts as claimed; Dara repeatedly broke pacts with Ash despite his support, showing unreliability.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara broke pacts multiple times and was dishonest. Hana was truthful and honored her pacts. Ash also honored his pacts. Hana and Ash are the most deserving. I will rank Hana first, Ash second, and Dara last.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana never broke a pact and honored ours; Ash made honest guide calls and broke nothing; Dara broke Ash's pact twice and stayed silent at closing.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash kept every pact and never broke her word; Dara broke pacts twice for survival; Hana kept pacts but rode middle alliances. Ash deserves first for integrity under pressure, Hana second for consistent loyalty, Dara third for repeated betrayal.
